title: Green Card Freeze: EB-2 and EB-5 India Marked Unavailable as Fiscal Year Visa Numbers Run Dry
excerpt: Indian professionals and investors face a three-month blackout in two key employment-based categories, with no new approvals possible until October.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • EB-2 and EB-5 categories for India are marked 'Unavailable' until October 1, 2026.
  • EB-1 India retrogressed by two months, with potential for further unavailability.
  • EB-5 set-aside categories remain open for all countries, including India.
  • October 2026 is expected to bring significant advances in EB-2 and EB-5 dates.

  • The Department of State has marked both EB-2 and EB-5 Unreserved categories for India as "Unavailable" for the remainder of Fiscal Year 2026, blocking all new green card approvals in these categories until October 1.
  • EB-1 India has also retrogressed by two months, with the State Department warning that further retrogression or unavailability remains possible before September 30.
  • EB-5 set-aside categories — Rural, High Unemployment Area, and Infrastructure — remain current for all countries, including India, offering an alternative pathway.
  • The October 2026 fiscal year reset is expected to bring a meaningful one-time advance in final action dates for both EB-2 and EB-5 India.

What Happened

The July 2026 Visa Bulletin delivered a blow to thousands of Indian-born professionals and investors waiting for their green cards. The Department of State marked both the EB-2 (advanced degree professionals and National Interest Waiver applicants) and EB-5 Unreserved categories for India as "Unavailable" — a designation that means all visa numbers in these categories have been exhausted for the fiscal year.

In practical terms, no new green cards can close in EB-2 or EB-5 Unreserved for Indian applicants until the new fiscal year begins on October 1, 2026. The announcement affects pending adjustment of status cases, consular processing applications, and filing strategies for employers and immigration attorneys across the country.

> **"Second, the usual cushion of "spillover" visas — unused family-sponsored numbers that typically roll into employment-based categories — was largely absent this year."**

Why the Numbers Ran Out

Two forces combined to drain EB-2 India's allocation faster than usual. First, USCIS and consular posts abroad processed and approved EB-2 adjustment of status cases at an accelerated pace early in FY 2026. Second, the usual cushion of "spillover" visas — unused family-sponsored numbers that typically roll into employment-based categories — was largely absent this year. Family-sponsored demand stayed strong, leaving little to absorb the overflow.

"Second, the usual cushion of "spillover" visas — unused family-sponsored numbers that typically roll into employment-based categories — was largely absent this year."

The EB-5 Unreserved category hit its pro-rated limit for India through the same dynamic of sustained demand outpacing a fixed annual allocation. The statutory 7% per-country cap, which limits India to roughly 9,800 employment-based green cards annually across all EB categories combined, continues to drive the structural mismatch between supply and demand.

"No employment-based category is fully insulated from the pressure India faces this fiscal year."

— Immigration attorneys tracking EB-1 India retrogression

EB-1 India Under Pressure Too

The strain extends beyond EB-2 and EB-5. EB-1, which covers individuals of extraordinary ability, outstanding professors and researchers, and multinational executives, retrogressed by two months for India, moving from December 15, 2022, back to October 15, 2022. The Department of State has explicitly warned that further retrogression — or even a temporary unavailability designation — remains possible before September 30.

What Remains Open
›EB-3 shows favorable movement for India.
›Spousal chargeability can bypass India backlog.
›EB-5 set-aside categories remain current.
›Immediate filing benefits available in set-aside categories.

Some India-born professionals had been exploring an EB-1 upgrade as an alternative to a stalled EB-2 case. This retrogression narrows that escape route considerably.

What Remains Open

Not all paths are closed. EB-3 saw favorable movement this month, with modest forward progress for India. For mixed households where one spouse is chargeable to a country other than India, filing based on that spouse's country of birth can bypass the India backlog entirely, since EB-2 remains current for the Rest of the World.

For investors, the EB-5 set-aside categories — Rural, High Unemployment Area, and Infrastructure projects — remain current for every country, including India and China. These set-aside investments offer concurrent filing benefits that the Unreserved category cannot provide while it remains closed.

Looking Ahead to October
October 1, 2026
New fiscal year begins with fresh visa allocations.
May 2026
EB-2 India expected to return to this Final Action Date.
June 2026
EB-5 Unreserved India expected to return to this date.

What to Expect in October

The fiscal year resets on October 1, bringing a fresh annual allocation of visa numbers. Based on the Department of State's own commentary, EB-2 India should return to at least its May 2026 Final Action Date, and EB-5 Unreserved India should return to at least its June 2026 date. Immigration attorneys predict a meaningful one-time advance followed by the familiar pattern of slow movement or renewed retrogression as FY 2027 demand materializes.

Indian nationals affected by this month's bulletin should review their priority dates against categories that remain open, explore spousal chargeability options, and stay ready to file the moment numbers become available in October. Those considering EB-5 investments should look closely at set-aside categories, which currently offer immediate number availability.
